title: Game profile
description: One game's profile in the game database (data/games/<id>.json). The id is the file name. Optional fields are omitted when empty or at their default. See README.md, 'Contributing to the game database'.

name.description: The game's name as the stores show it.

description.description: One sentence on what the game is, shown only in the database browser: modes, perspective, genres and series in PCGamingWiki's pattern ("X is a singleplayer first-person shooter game in the Y series."), in our own words. Starts with the game's name. Doesn't repeat what other fields (e.g. store_details) say, such as what a bundle includes.

released.description: When the game first came out on Windows (earliest region), as YYYY-MM-DD. Use YYYY-MM or YYYY if that's all you can confirm. Bundles and Gold, Complete, GOTY or Classic editions use the base game's date; Enhanced Editions, Remasters and Anniversary Editions use their own.

exe.description: The game's main program file, with its exact capitalisation and no folders, e.g. "DeusEx.exe". The script uses it to recognise the right folder.

stores.description: Where the game is sold. Leave a store out if the game isn't sold there.

eax.description: How the game plays 3D audio, which EAX versions it supports, and whether EAX works in the current build.

versions.description: The EAX versions the game supports, from a source you can check.

status.description: Where EAX stands today: supported; removed_by_patch (an update took EAX out of the current build); not_implemented (a remaster or rewrite that never had EAX); built_in (EAX already works in this build without the script, for example because the game ships its own OpenAL32.dll with EAX).

problem.description: Why the current build isn't simply supported, in plain words, matching the status above.

fix.description: How to get a build where EAX works.

fix_in_place.description: Tick this when the fix works on the install the script is already pointed at (for example a Steam beta branch), so the script warns and offers to continue instead of stopping.

install.description: What the install does differently for this game.

tweaks.description: Advanced Compatibility Tweaks the script recommends for this game; each is asked as a Yes/No question that defaults to Yes.

alsoft_ini.description: Extra OpenAL Soft settings to offer on top of the generated alsoft.ini, as section, key, value. Only the keys the editor lists are accepted.

game_config.description: Changes to the game's own config files, offered to the player in the Game Settings step.

audio_settings.description: Settings that turn on EAX and 3D sound, or make them sound right, so the player doesn't have to change them by hand.

optional_settings.description: Extras that aren't needed for EAX, such as sharper textures. The player picks which to apply.

sources.description: Pages that back up this profile's claims. They're listed as links at the bottom of the game's profile screen. Each is a web address, or a title with an address to show a name instead of the address.

notes.description: Anything worth telling the player that the other fields don't cover.

id.description: The store's ID for the game (Steam AppID or GOG game ID), checked against the store. For GOG, use the ID Heroic installs it under (its appName, the same as the gameId in the game's goggame-<id>.info). For a game sold inside a pack or collection, use the game's own ID, never the pack's.

delisted.description: The game is no longer on sale; people who already own it keep access.

api.description: The audio API for this store's build only, instead of the game's usual one.

beta_branch.description: Steam only: the beta branch name that brings EAX back.

extra_exe_folders.description: GOG only: other folders inside the game's exe folder that have an exe of their own (for example expansions started from the same title). They get the same files as the main folder.

companion_apps.description: Steam only: IDs of other Steam apps that run this game's exe from its folder (for example DOOM 3's Resurrection of Evil, 9070, which starts Doom3.exe with its own options). Each has its own Wine/Proton prefix and launch options, which the install sets up like the game's own.

store_details.description: What's different about this store's listing. Don't mention an Enhanced Edition, remaster or remake of a game that isn't one, unless the store sells them together; then name every game in it.

name_part.description: The name of a config section or key.

registry_key.description: A registry path, written with single backslashes as it appears under its hive in the prefix's .reg file, for example Software\Wow6432Node\Outrage\Descent3.

value.description: Text sets the value (for a registry number, a decimal number). true or false switches a NewDark flag on or off. null removes the key.

format.description: ini: [Section] then key=value. flat_ini: key=value lines with no sections. idtech_cfg: seta key "value". dark_cfg: NewDark "key value" lines, where a bare key is a flag that's on and ;key turns it off. brace_cfg: {key} = {value} lines (Fallout Tactics' bos.cfg). ltx: key value lines with no sections (S.T.A.L.K.E.R.'s user.ltx). gadb: Monolith's binary profile (F.E.A.R.'s Profile000.gdb); it can only switch an existing on/off setting, so values are "0" or "1". wine_reg: the prefix's system.reg or user.reg, for a game that keeps its options in the registry; only numbers and text can be changed, a number as a decimal.

locations.description: Where to look for the file, in order, written as "base:path". The first one that exists is used. A registry file can only be prefix:system.reg or prefix:user.reg.

if_missing.description: What to do when none of the locations exist. Leave empty to ask the player to launch the game once and check again; skip to leave this file's part out of each setting and tell the player; create to create the file.

crash_marker.description: A file in the same folder that the game creates while it runs and deletes when it quits normally. If it's left behind, the game resets this config file the next time it starts, so the script removes it (when the game isn't running) before changing this file. It isn't put back on uninstall.

title.description: Starts with Enable, Fix, Remove or Raise, then the result, for example "Enable EAX reverb".

reason.description: What the game does out of the box, in one or two short sentences.

only_if.description: When to offer the setting. If the conditions aren't met it's skipped without a message.

speakers.description: Offer only for these answers to the Speaker Configuration question: stereo, headphones (Stereo, then Headphones), matrix, surround (any surround layout), or one exact layout (quad, surround51, surround61, surround71). A list matches any of its values.

changes.description: What to change. ini files: file, section, key, value. Other text files: file, key, value. Registry files: file, registry key, value name, value. Every file must first be defined under game_config.files.

follow_up.description: Something the player should do after installing. It's shown in the final summary.
